claim: Organizations has two broad categories of policy: authorization policies (SCPs and RCPs) manage the security of accounts, and declarative policies configure and manage AWS services and their features across the organization.
question: Which categories of organization policy exist, and what does each category do?

values.display: centrally manage the security of AWS accounts
centrally configure and manage AWS services
service control policies (SCPs) and resource control policies (RCPs)

evidence.quote: Authorization policies help you to centrally manage the security of AWS accounts across an organization.
Declarative policies help you centrally configure and manage AWS services and their features across an organization.
There are two different types of authorization policies in AWS Organizations: service control policies (SCPs) and resource control policies (RCPs).

claim: SCPs are principal-centric controls that limit the maximum permissions of principals in member accounts; RCPs are resource-centric controls that limit the maximum permissions available for resources in member accounts.
question: What is the difference between an SCP and an RCP?

evidence.quote: SCPs are principal-centric controls. SCPs create a permissions guardrail, or set limits, on the maximum permissions available to principals in your member accounts.
RCPs are resource-centric controls. RCPs create a permissions guardrail, or set limits, on the maximum permissions available for resources in your member accounts.

claim: RCPs can affect the effective permissions of principals outside the organization that access your resources, while SCPs can affect only principals inside the organization.
question: Which authorization policy type can limit access by principals outside the organization?

values.display: principals external to your organization that are accessing your resources
SCPs can only impact the effective permissions

evidence.quote: RCPs provide an ability to impact the effective permissions for principals external to your organization that are accessing your resources. SCPs can only impact the effective permissions for principals within your AWS organization.

claim: SCPs and RCPs are independent controls; you can enable either one or both, and using both builds a data perimeter around your identities and your resources.
question: Do SCPs and RCPs depend on each other, and what do they build together?

values.display: SCPs and RCPs are independent controls
create a data perimeter around your identities and your resources

evidence.quote: SCPs and RCPs are independent controls. You can choose to enable only SCPs or RCPs, or use both policy types together. By using both SCPs and RCPs, you can create a data perimeter around your identities and your resources.

claim: SCPs control which resources your identities can access, for example to stop your identities from reaching resources outside the organization; RCPs control which identities can access your resources, for example to stop external identities.
question: Which question does an SCP answer and which question does an RCP answer?

values.display: control which resources your identities can access
control which identities can access your resources

evidence.quote: SCPs provide an ability to control which resources your identities can access.
RCPs provide an ability to control which identities can access your resources.

claim: You can replace FullAWSAccess with an SCP that allows only a set of services, so that new AWS services are not allowed until the SCPs are updated to allow them explicitly.
question: How does an allow-list SCP strategy work, and what does it do to new AWS services?

values.display: You can replace FullAWSAccess with a policy
new AWS services are not allowed

evidence.quote: You can replace FullAWSAccess with a policy allowing only a set of services so that new AWS services are not allowed unless they are explicitly allowed by updating SCPs.

claim: Disabling the SCP policy type in a root detaches all SCPs from every entity in that root; if SCPs are enabled again, only FullAWSAccess is attached and the old attachments are lost.
question: What happens to attached SCPs when the SCP policy type is disabled and enabled again?

values.display: are lost and aren't automatically recoverable

evidence.quote: When you disable the SCP policy type in a root, all SCPs are automatically detached from all AWS Organizations entities in that root.
Any attachments of SCPs to AWS Organizations entities from before SCPs were disabled are lost and aren't automatically recoverable, although you can manually reattach them.

claim: SCPs cannot restrict actions performed by the management account or actions performed with the permissions of a service-linked role.
question: Which tasks can SCPs not restrict?

values.display: Any action performed by the management account
permissions that are attached to a service-linked role

evidence.quote: You can't use SCPs to restrict the following tasks:
evidence.heading: Tasks and entities not restricted by SCPs

evidence.quote: Any action performed by the management account
evidence.heading: Tasks and entities not restricted by SCPs

evidence.quote: Any action performed using permissions that are attached to a service-linked role
evidence.heading: Tasks and entities not restricted by SCPs
